references.text: Describes the procedure for the burnt offering (עֹלָה) mentioned in Leviticus 5:10
The context of the offering with two turtledoves or two young doves, where one is a sin offering and the other is a burnt offering
Parallel formulation regarding the priest's atonement (וְכִפֶּר) and forgiveness (וְנִסְלַח)
The same concluding formula: the priest makes atonement, and the sin is forgiven
Repetition of the atonement and forgiveness formula as in 5:10
Concluding formula with atonement and forgiveness, identical structure
Parallel conclusion to the offering section with atonement and forgiveness
Similar formulation regarding the priest's atonement for sin
Repeats the theme of atonement and forgiveness for unintentional sin
The priest makes atonement with the offering, and the person is forgiven
Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
Contrast: the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins, pointing to Christ's perfect sacrifice
